result.narrative:
Vodafone Idea sits in the Watch band at a score of 25.5, driven in roughly two-thirds by a deteriorating payment record and one-third by negative news on its core business. The one open overdue on policy TCI-SCF-2026-0001 (INR 9.0M of a INR 120M limit) is 18 days past due, and the trend across the last two resolved episodes (5 days late in March, 9 in July) shows each cycle getting slower, with notification frequency also ticking up from one to two in the trailing six months. On the news side, the dominant item is a severity-2 story on Vodafone Idea's quarter-on-quarter subscriber decline, a genuine negative fundamental trend rather than an acute event, and it is reinforced by a same-severity earnings-miss article on a wider-than-expected Q2 loss that was not itself selected for the score but corroborates the picture. Against this, more recent coverage includes an analyst note acknowledging the company is "turning a corner" (severity 1) and a run of stock-price and financing items (including a $3.5bn SBI-led debt package) that are neutral-to-positive and carry no weight in the score.

The Watch band is reached because both legs of the formula point the same direction: a single, still-early-stage (1-30 day bucket) overdue combined with a worsening resolution pattern, plus credible negative sector/earnings news on the same name. The adjudicator agreed with the score but flagged caveats: the deteriorating payment trajectory could push the buyer into High Risk before the next review if it continues, the exposure is entirely concentrated on one policy/insurer with no cross-policy confirmation, and the published news score may understate total negative coverage since only the single highest-severity article is counted.

The recommended limit action is to maintain the current INR 120M limit on policy TCI-SCF-2026-0001, as the probability of default (15.52%) remains within the target appetite (25%) and both expected loss before and after are unchanged at INR 13,409,280. No change in exposure is proposed at this time, but given the adjudicator's caveats this should be treated as a limit to monitor rather than a clean pass.

A move to the better Healthy band would need the score to fall by 5.5 points, consistent with the overdue clearing and the payment trend reverting to the faster resolution times seen earlier in the year, alongside the negative news aging out or being offset by positive coverage. Conversely, a move to High Risk (50.0, 24.5 points away) would likely follow if the current overdue extends to around 43 days past due, if further notifications or a repeat overdue appear on the same policy, or if additional severity-2-or-higher news (such as the uncounted earnings-miss article) continues to accumulate alongside the subscriber-decline story.
